## Natural history notes

A small cellar spider characterized by its very long, thin legs, pale brown to grayish body, and distinctive boxy abdomen with a small rear “tail-like” projection. In Florida, it is found mostly in and around human structures, including houses, sheds, garages, porches, crawlspaces, and other sheltered areas where it builds loose, irregular webs. It feeds on small insects and other arthropods caught in its web and, like other cellar spiders, may vibrate rapidly when disturbed.
